children: Walt Disney stock is showing signs of life after a lost decade for the House of Mouse.
Shares have rallied 15% over the past three months, closing at $113.11 on Monday — just $4 shy of their 52-week high.
That suggests Wall Street is getting behind CEO Josh D'Amaro's growth plan, which centers on pouring money into technology and supercharging growth for the Disney+ streaming service.

Cutting costs are also part of the turnaround effort. Disney is moving toward thousands of job cuts, with some managers asked to target slashing annual costs by 20%, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Disney didn't immediately respond to a request for comment from Barron's. Its stock slid 0.6% to $112.47 in early trading on Tuesday.

Other entertainment companies, including Netflix, have also laid off staff this year, as streamers struggle to accelerate growth as the likes of TikTok and Alphabet's YouTube ramp up the battle for user engagement.

But the stakes may be even higher for D'Amaro. Shares of Disney have floundered for more than a decade at this point, due to massive subscriber losses at ESPN, so the recent rally is a welcome development.
Barron's in January laid out a road map to fix Disney, calling for it to accelerate streaming growth, revive films' box-office performance, sort out ESPN, and build on recent theme-park success.
Cutting costs by laying off staff didn't make our to-do list, but the question now is whether the savings can help sustain Disney's turnaround.
